article.cgnat.step.check.copy.range: Address range providers use for CGNAT
article.cgnat.step.check.text: Compare two addresses. Open your router's status page and note its internet (WAN) address. Then run the public address check in Diagnostics. If they differ, or the router's address starts with 100.64 up to 100.127, you are behind CGNAT.
article.cgnat.step.options.text: You have three options: use a VPN that connects out from your home (such as Tailscale), use a relay, or ask your provider for a public address, which some provide on request or for a fee.
article.cgnat.step.what.text: Some internet providers share one public address between many homes. This is called carrier-grade NAT, or CGNAT. Nothing outside can reach a port on your router, so port forwarding cannot work.
article.cgnat.summary: Why some homes cannot be reached from outside.
article.cgnat.title: CGNAT
article.codecs_bandwidth.step.codecs.tex: Cameras send H.264 or H.265 (HEVC). H.265 is smaller but needs more from your phone. If video stutters, switch the camera to H.264 or choose its substream.
article.codecs_bandwidth.step.mobile.tex: On mobile data, watch the substream and few cameras at once, or video will use a lot of your data allowance.
article.codecs_bandwidth.step.speed.text: Away from home, the limit is your home internet's upload speed. All the streams you watch share it.
Most cameras offer a main stream (sharp, heavy) and a substream (smaller, light). The grid uses the substream and fullscreen uses the main stream.
article.codecs_bandwidth.summary: Why video stutters, and what to change.
article.codecs_bandwidth.title: Codecs and bandwidth
article.ddns_forward.step.add.text: In Roehens, use the dynamic DNS name as the address and your external port as the port.
article.ddns_forward.step.cgnat.text: Check that your internet provider gives your router its own public address. If it does not, this path cannot work.
article.ddns_forward.step.ddns.text: Create a dynamic DNS name in your router or camera. The name keeps pointing at your home even when your provider changes your address.
article.ddns_forward.step.forward.callou: Never forward the camera's web admin page or its ONVIF port.
article.ddns_forward.step.forward.copy.r: Camera RTSP port (the port to forward to)
article.ddns_forward.step.forward.text: In your router, forward one external port to the camera's fixed address and RTSP port. Choose an uncommon external port.
article.ddns_forward.step.test.text: Switch this phone to mobile data and run the test. It must work away from your Wi-Fi to count.
article.ddns_forward.step.warning.text: This path opens one port of your router to the camera. Use it only if a VPN is not possible, and read the port security article first.
article.ddns_forward.summary: Reach one camera through a name that follows your home address.
article.ddns_forward.title: DDNS and port forward
article.lan_setup.step.add.text: Add the camera in Roehens with its address and port, then run the connection test.
article.lan_setup.step.check.text: If the test fails, its result says which step failed. The troubleshooter can take it from there.
article.lan_setup.step.enable.copy.onvif: Usual ONVIF port (some cameras use 8000 or 8080)
article.lan_setup.step.enable.text: In the camera's own settings, turn on RTSP. Turn on ONVIF too if you want pan and tilt. If the camera allows it, create a separate user just for viewing.
article.lan_setup.step.find.text: Find the camera's address. Roehens can look for it, or you can read it in your router's list of connected devices.
article.lan_setup.step.network.text: Connect this phone and the camera to the same router. Wi-Fi and a network cable both work, as long as they are on the same home network.
article.lan_setup.step.reserve.callout: A camera whose address changes stops working in Roehens until you update the address.
article.lan_setup.step.reserve.text: In your router, give the camera a fixed address. This is often called address reservation or static DHCP. The camera then keeps the same address after a restart.
article.lan_setup.summary: Set up a camera on your home network.
article.lan_setup.title: Same Wi-Fi
article.port_security.step.passwords.tex: Change the default password of the camera and of the router. Use a long, unique password.
article.port_security.step.scope.text: Forward only the RTSP port. Do not forward the camera's web admin page or its ONVIF port, and turn off UPnP in the router so nothing opens ports by itself.
article.port_security.step.updates.text: Install firmware updates for the camera and the router. Old camera firmware is a common way in.
article.port_security.step.vpn.text: A VPN needs no camera port open to the internet. If you can use one, do.
article.port_security.step.watch.callout: Roehens never opens ports for you and sends nothing to a server of its own.
article.port_security.step.watch.text: Check from time to time that no extra ports are forwarded in your router.
article.port_security.summary: Keep an opened port from becoming a way in.
article.port_security.title: Port security
Web page and many snapshot or MJPEG streams
ONVIF on many cameras (others use 80 or 8080)
article.port_selection.step.inside.text: Inside your home, use the ports your camera already listens on.
article.port_selection.step.outside.call: A forward from external port 18554 to camera port 554 is fine. Roehens then uses 18554.
article.port_selection.step.outside.text: For a forwarded port, choose an external port that is not a well-known one. Numbers from 10000 to 60000 are a good range. The external port may differ from the camera port.
article.port_selection.step.unique.text: Use a different external port for each camera or recorder. Ports run from 1 to 65535.
article.port_selection.summary: Choose ports that work and attract less attention.
article.port_selection.title: Port selection
article.relay.step.add.text: In Roehens, use that address and port for the camera.
article.relay.step.kinds.text: Relays come in two kinds: cloud services offered by some camera makers, and general tunnel services that forward a port. Names such as ngrok are examples of the second kind and are not an endorsement.
article.relay.step.limits.text: Relays often limit speed, add delay, or allow only some stream types. If video is slow, try the substream.
article.relay.step.setup.text: Set the relay up by following its own instructions. It gives you an address and a port for your camera.
article.relay.step.what.callout: Video then passes through the relay. Read its privacy terms. Roehens does not run, test or recommend any relay.
article.relay.step.what.text: A relay is a service in between: your camera or a small device at home connects out to the service, and your phone connects to the service. No port of your router is opened.
article.relay.summary: Use a service that carries the video for you.
article.relay.title: Third-party relay
article.router_notes.step.brands_a.text: TP-Link: Advanced, then NAT Forwarding, then Virtual Servers. ASUS: WAN, then Virtual Server or Port Forwarding. Netgear: Advanced, then Advanced Setup, then Port Forwarding.
article.router_notes.step.brands_b.text: D-Link: Features or Advanced, then Port Forwarding or Virtual Server. Linksys: Security, then Apps and Gaming. MikroTik: IP, then Firewall, then NAT, with chain dstnat. UniFi: Settings, then Routing and Firewall, then Port Forwarding.
article.router_notes.step.names.callout: Look for a list where you can add a rule with an external port, an internal address and an internal port.
article.router_notes.step.names.text: Port forwarding is also called Virtual Server, NAT forwarding or Applications and Gaming. Menu names change between models and firmware versions, so use these as a starting point.
article.router_notes.step.reserve.text: Set the camera's fixed address first, in the same router, so the forward keeps pointing at it.
article.router_notes.summary: Where to find port forwarding on common routers.
article.router_notes.title: Router notes
article.static_ip_forward.step.add.text: In Roehens, use your public address as the address and your external port as the port.
article.static_ip_forward.step.address.t: Ask your internet provider for a fixed public address, or check that the one you have does not change. You can see your current address in Diagnostics.
article.static_ip_forward.step.forward.c: Never forward the camera's web admin page or its ONVIF port.
Camera RTSP port (the port to forward to)
article.static_ip_forward.step.forward.t: In your router, forward one external port to the camera's fixed address and RTSP port. Choose an uncommon external port.
article.static_ip_forward.step.test.text: Switch this phone to mobile data and run the test. It must work away from your Wi-Fi to count.
article.static_ip_forward.step.warning.t: This path opens one port of your router to the camera. Use it only if a VPN is not possible, and read the port security article first.
article.static_ip_forward.summary: Reach one camera through a fixed public address.
article.static_ip_forward.title: Static IP and port forward
article.vpn.step.choose.text: Pick one. WireGuard is fast and simple and runs on many routers or on a small always-on computer. Tailscale is the easiest and needs no router changes. OpenVPN is supported by many routers.
article.vpn.step.connect.text: Turn the VPN on while you are on mobile data. Your phone now behaves as if it were at home.
article.vpn.step.phone.text: Install the VPN's app on this phone and sign in or import your connection file.
article.vpn.step.server.text: Set up the VPN at home by following the instructions of the VPN you chose. WireGuard and OpenVPN each listen on one port of your router.
article.vpn.step.use.callout: If video does not start, check that your home network's address range is included in the VPN.
article.vpn.step.use.text: Open Roehens and use the camera's normal home address. Nothing else needs to change.
article.vpn.step.why.text: A VPN connects your phone to your home network from anywhere. Your cameras stay private and are never opened to the internet. It is the safest way to watch away from home.
article.vpn.summary: Reach your cameras from anywhere without opening your router.
article.vpn.title: VPN
trouble.away_fails.answer.no: No, it is also slow or stutters at home
trouble.away_fails.question: Does it fail only when you are away from home, for example on mobile data?
trouble.forwarded.question: Have you forwarded a port on your router to the camera?
trouble.home_kind.answer.auth: It asks for a username or password
trouble.home_kind.answer.path: The stream path was not found
trouble.home_kind.answer.picture: It connects but there is no picture
trouble.home_kind.question: What does the connection test say?
trouble.out_auth.outcome: The camera refused the username or password. Check them in the camera settings, and make sure the user is allowed to view video. Then edit the camera in Roehens and test again.
trouble.out_cgnat.outcome: Your provider shares one public address between homes, so port forwarding cannot work. A VPN that connects out from your home, or a relay, can.
trouble.out_check.outcome: Check the two addresses first. Run Public address in Diagnostics and compare it with the internet address on your router's status page.
trouble.out_forward.outcome: Away from home you need a way in: a VPN is the safest, or a forwarded port with a dynamic DNS name or a fixed address.
trouble.out_forward_check.outcome: Check that the external port matches the one in Roehens, that the forward points at the camera's fixed address and RTSP port, and that no firewall blocks it.
trouble.out_path.outcome: The camera answered, but not on that path. Choose the camera brand in the camera form to try the paths that brand uses.
trouble.out_picture.outcome: The camera connects but video does not start. Try the substream, or switch the camera to H.264.
trouble.out_slow.outcome: Slow or stuttering video is usually the stream size. Use the substream, lower the camera bitrate, or try H.264.
trouble.out_unreachable.outcome: The phone cannot find the camera. Check that both are on the same network, that the address is right, and that the camera has a fixed address.
trouble.out_vpn.outcome: Check that the VPN is on, and that your home network's address range goes through it. Then use the camera's normal home address in Roehens.
trouble.shared_address.question: Is your router's internet address the same as the address shown by Public address in Diagnostics?
trouble.uses_vpn.question: Do you use a VPN to reach your home network?
trouble.wifi_works.answer.no: No, it does not play at home
trouble.wifi_works.question: Does the camera play in Roehens when this phone is on the same Wi-Fi as the camera?
